sources.title: Introducing Devin
sources.finding: Devin cloud provides shell, IDE and interactive browser tools; local CLI can hand work to cloud.

sources.title: Devin pricing
sources.finding: Free desktop access differs from Pro cloud access; Teams has a base fee plus full developer seats, while quota amounts are not fixed in the FAQ.

sources.title: Devin API overview
sources.finding: The v3 organization and enterprise APIs manage sessions and context resources with service users or personal tokens; attribution requires defined permissions.

sources.title: Security profiles
sources.finding: Security profiles separately restrict network, external MCP, Devin-management tools and Git writes; child sessions inherit the profile chain.

sources.title: Welcome to Devin Desktop
sources.finding: Devin Desktop installs on macOS, Windows and Linux; its primary local harness is Devin Local, shared with Devin CLI. A Devin account is required; cloud and local workflows remain distinct.

sources.title: Devin CLI Quickstart
sources.finding: Devin CLI runs locally on macOS, Linux and Windows. Cloud Devin runs in a VM. CLI currently does not support account Knowledge, Playbooks or Secrets; these are planned, not shipped.

sources.title: Devin Cloud in the Devin CLI
sources.locator: Start; Resume; Continue locally; Local Hands
sources.finding: Cloud sessions run on their own VM and continue when the terminal closes. Resume accepts a session URL/ID. Pickup checks out the PR branch locally; Local Hands requires per-call approval.

sources.title: Devin CLI Subagents
sources.locator: How Subagents Work; Cost; Model profiles
sources.finding: Foreground children wait with interactive approvals; background children run concurrently and deny unapproved tools. The parent receives completion and summarizes results. Each child has independent inference costs and profile-selected model.

sources.title: Devin Knowledge
sources.finding: Knowledge stores shared instructions, supports trigger retrieval and repo/organization/enterprise scope, user toggles and corrections. It is deprecated and gradually migrating to Skills in Plugins; future removal has no stated date.

sources.title: Session Insights
sources.finding: Completed sessions have free Insights with usage, message count, size classification, issue timeline and knowledge analysis. Full large-session analysis is automatic; smaller sessions can request analysis through UI or API.

sources.title: Devin Review
sources.locator: Features; Reading a Review; PR Workflow Actions; Permissions
sources.finding: Devin Review displays grouped diffs, supports comments and request changes, retains analyses and CI status, and offers provider-dependent PR workflow actions. Write actions require appropriate connected identities and permissions.

sources.title: Security at Cognition
sources.locator: Privacy and IP; Retention; Third-party audits
sources.finding: Cognition states SOC 2 Type II since September 2024. Training is on by default except Enterprise without written consent; paid users can opt out. Customer data is retained during the relationship, while interaction/feedback retention is separately determined.

sources.title: Devin Plans and Pricing
sources.finding: Free desktop access has a light agent quota. Pro costs $20/month, Max $200. Teams charge $80/month plus $40/full-development seat. Paid usage allowances refresh daily and weekly; extra usage is at API pricing.

sources.title: Welcome to Devin Desktop
sources.locator: Set Up > Linux deb/rpm repository notes; Uninstall > Windows pre-rename folder note
sources.finding: Vendor explicitly calls windsurf repository names pre-rebrand, names devin-desktop as the new package, and retains a transitional windsurf package for existing installs. Windows installations from before the rename may retain a Windsurf folder. This establishes the editor lineage, not a former name for Devin cloud.
